checks.reason: X_m=g_delta A(Y_(m,J)) with Y_(m,J)(f)=W(Q_J T_(delta,m)f) on one W. Joint Gaussianity comes from common first-chaos membership. Block independence appears nowhere, and the only independence used is orthogonal Gaussian head/tail in Section 3.

checks.claim: Section 2 all-p moment bound (6), mean bound (7) and second moment hold uniformly in m, J and delta.
checks.reason: The isometric pullback and contraction Q_J give Var Y<=||f||^2. Source-operator Theorem 1 with C=1 then transfers the actual-driver sqrt(p) bound (4) at T=B. The bounded map M->iM L_psi gives the F extension, and stopping does not raise the Holder norm. Delta n<2/B holds because delta<1/B. Jensen plus linearity gives (7), and the L^(2/p) triangle inequality gives EY^2<infinity. C depends only on the allowed fixed data.

checks.claim: Bochner conditional expectations are built without RNP, the norming family is countable, and raw-Gaussian regression gives X_n with L2 convergence.
checks.reason: The simple-variable definition, conditional norm inequality and scalar Jensen give an L2 contraction. Hahn-Banach on a dense unit sequence gives a countable norming family generating the Borel sets. Regression gives ell(E[X|G_n])=sum W(e_i)<k_ell,e_i>=ell(sum W(e_i)L e_i), which is (8). X_n->X follows by the three-term argument: simple variables measurable in the union algebra are dense, E[S|G_n]=S eventually, and the contraction controls the rest. No Hilbert-valued or trace-class raw Gaussian is used.

checks.claim: The H_seen quotient and Cameron norm (9) are correct.
checks.reason: By (2) and Hahn-Banach, ker L=H_seen^perp, and L is injective on H_seen. The closed first chaos of X is W(H_seen). E[X W(Phi)]=L Phi matches the source definition of H with norm (E Z^2)^(1/2). So (1) bounds the true embedding H_CM->E_delta by sqrt(delta)s.

checks.claim: Closed support equals E0, including the degenerate law, using only orthogonal head/tail independence and finite-dimensional head full support.
checks.reason: X lies in E0 almost surely as a limit of X_n. The tail statistics W((I-P_n)k_ell) are orthogonal to e_1,...,e_n, and the Borel family is countable, so the Banach tail is independent of the head. The coefficient-ball preimage has positive standard Gaussian measure, and the rho/3 argument gives every L Phi in the support. Closure completes the claim, and E0={0} is routed to the zero case.

checks.claim: The measurable-norm criterion holds uniformly over finite orthonormal families in F_n-perp.
checks.reason: h_j in H_seen with h_j orthogonal to P_seen e_i gives <h_j,e_i>=0. Then <(I-P_n)k_ell,h_j>=<k_ell,h_j>=ell(L h_j), which gives (10) by regression. Conditional Jensen bounds E||Z_G||^2 independently of the family. Chebyshev with right side <epsilon^3 gives tail <epsilon, and n depends only on epsilon. This is Gross's condition with the finite-dimensional F_n.

checks.claim: The completion and characteristic law give an abstract Wiener realization without circularity.
checks.reason: The law already exists from C3, so measurable-norm verification is not a construction premise. The completion of H_CM in ||.||_delta is E0 by definition of E0. The dual norm is sup_{||Phi||<=1}<k_ell,Phi>=||k_ell||, which matches exp(-||k_ell||^2/2). H_CM is dense and continuously embedded, and E0 is separable with centered Radon law. Borell is not used before Section 4, and the driver/moment inputs do not depend on this note.
